source_text: Μετέπειτα δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν ἡγεμόνα ἀχθέντων αὐτῶν κἀκείνου πάσῃ τῇ πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὠμότητι χρωμένου, Οὐέττιος Ἐπάγαθος, εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν, πλήρωμα ἀγάπης τῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν πλησίον κεχωρηκώς, οὗ καὶ ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ἠκρίβωτο ἡ πολιτεία, ὡς καίπερ ὄντα νέον συνεξισοῦσθαι τῇ τοῦ πρεσβυτέρου Ζαχαρίου μαρτυρίᾳ· πεπόρευτο γοῦν ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασι τοῦ κυρίου ἄμεμπτος καὶ πάσῃ τῇ πρὸς τὸν πλησίον λειτουργίᾳ ἄοκνος, ζῆλον θεοῦ πολὺν ἔχων καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι· τοιοῦτος δή τις ὤν, τὴν οὕτως καθ᾽ ἡμῶν ἀλόγως γινομένην κρίσιν οὐκ ἐβάστασεν, ἀλλ᾽ ὑπερηγανάκτησε, καὶ ἠξίου καὶ αὐτὸς ἀκουσθῆναι ἀπολογούμενος ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὅτι μηδὲν ἄθεον μηδὲ ἀσεβὲς ἐστιν ἐν ἡμῖν. Τῶν δὲ περὶ τὸ βῆμα καταβοησάντων αὐτοῦ, καὶ γὰρ ἦν ἐπίσημος, καὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος μὴ ἀνασχομένου τῆς οὕτως ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ δικαίας προταθείσης ἀξιώσεως, ἀλλὰ μόνον τοῦτο πυθομένου εἰ καὶ αὐτὸς εἴη Χριστιανός, τοῦ δὲ λαμπροτάτῃ φωνῇ ὁμολογήσαντος, ἀνελήφθη καὶ αὐτὸς εἰς τὸν κλῆρον τῶν μαρτύρων, παράκλητος Χριστιανῶν χρηματίσας, ἔχων δὲ τὸν παράκλητον ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ Ζαχαρίου, ὃ διὰ τοῦ πληρώματος τῆς ἀγάπης ἐνεδείξατο, εὐδοκήσας ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἀπολογίας καὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν· ἦν γὰρ καὶ ἔστιν γνήσιος Χριστοῦ μαθητής, ἀκολουθῶν τῷ ἀρνίῳ ὅπου ἂν ὑπάγῃ.
pass_a_gloss: Later, when they were led to the governor and he was employing all harshness toward us, Vettius Epagathus, one from the brethren, having attained full measure of love toward God and toward neighbor, whose conduct had been exacted to such a degree that although young he was made equal to the testimony of the presbyter Zacharius; for he had walked blameless in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord and untiring in all service toward neighbor, having much zeal for God and burning in spirit; being such a one, he did not bear the judgment coming irrationally against us, but was greatly indignant, and demanded also himself to be heard making defense for the brethren that nothing atheistic nor impious is in us. But those around the tribunal shouted him down, for he was prominent, and the governor did not endure the just proposition put forward by him, but only asked this, whether he himself also is a Christian, and he having confessed with most radiant voice, he also was taken up into the lot of the martyrs, having been called advocate of Christians, but having the Advocate in himself, the spirit of Zacharias, which through the fullness of love he displayed, consenting for the defense of the brethren even to give his own soul; for he was and is a genuine disciple of Christ, following the Lamb wherever it goes.
pass_b_english: Afterward, when they were brought before the governor and he dealt with us with every harshness, Vettius Epagathus, one of the brethren who had reached the full measure of love toward God and toward neighbor, stood out. His life had been so exact that, young as he was, he was ranked equal with the testimony borne to the elder Zacharias, for he walked in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless (Luke 1:6), and was untiring in every service to his neighbor, holding great zeal for God and burning in spirit. Being such a man, he could not endure the senseless judgment pronounced against us, but was filled with indignation and demanded that he too be heard in defense of the brethren, that there is nothing atheistic or impious among us.

But the crowd around the tribunal cried him down, for he was a man of standing, and the governor would not accept the just proposal he had made, but asked him only this, whether he himself was a Christian. When he confessed in a most ringing voice, he too was taken up into the company of the martyrs, called the advocate of the Christians, while having the Advocate within himself, the Spirit (John 14:16-17), the spirit of Zacharias, which he displayed through the fullness of love, consenting for the sake of the defense of the brethren to lay down his own life. For he was and is a genuine disciple of Christ, following the Lamb wherever he goes (Revelation 14:4).

choices.why: Legal context of tribunal, defense plea, and demand to be heard points to advocate rather than comforter; χρηματίσας marks a public role taken.

choices.term: τὸν παράκλητον ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τὸ πνεῦμα
choices.english: the Advocate within himself, the Spirit
choices.why: Second use shifts inward and is identified as spirit, echoing the Johannine Paraclete dwelling in believers, distinct from his forensic role.
Consent unto death for the brethren requires life, not merely soul as inner self.
